obligation: Report actual or threatened cyber incident (Coast Guard, FBI, CISA)
trigger: Evidence of an actual or threatened cyber incident involving or endangering either terminal, including its data, networks and systems (for example a ransom note, encryption of TOS or gate servers, an unapproved session on a crane controller, or a compromised vendor account)
deadline: Immediately
notify: FBI (local field office), CISA (cisa.gov/report) and the Captain of the Port for each affected terminal (T1 and T2 are in different COTP zones; Sector command center numbers in each FSP and incident binder)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - both terminals are waterfront facilities with FSPs. CySO reports; alternate CySO or the terminal FSO if the CySO cannot be reached (POL-03 4.4)

obligation: Reportable cyber incident to the National Response Center (fallback)
trigger: A reportable cyber incident (for example substantial loss of availability of a covered system, or disruption of business operations) that has not been reported to the Coast Guard under 6.16-1
deadline: Without delay
notify: National Response Center, 1-800-424-8802
applies_at_this_tier: Only if no report was made under 6.16-1. A 6.16-1 report to the Coast Guard satisfies this duty

trigger: Activities that may result in a transportation security incident (for example signs that attackers are targeting PACS, CCTV or crane controllers)
deadline: Without delay
notify: National Response Center, 1-800-424-8802
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - terminal FSO decides under the FSP

citation: 33 CFR 101.305(b); breach of security defined in 101.105
trigger: Security measures circumvented, eluded or violated without a TSI (for example TWIC access control, PACS or CCTV disabled by the attack)
deadline: Without delay
notify: National Response Center, 1-800-424-8802
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if FSP security measures are affected - terminal FSO decides

trigger: A security incident resulting in significant loss of life, environmental damage, transportation system disruption or economic disruption in the area (for example a multi-day closure of a terminal, or an injury caused by manipulated crane controls)
deadline: Without delay, then follow the FSP procedures
notify: Captain of the Port for the affected terminal (the FSP may also call for the National Response Center)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the incident reaches TSI level - FSO and terminal General Manager decide with the COTP

obligation: Record the incident and any cyber threat
trigger: Any reportable cyber incident, security incident, breach of security or security threat
deadline: Create during the incident; keep at least 2 years, protected against unauthorized deletion, destruction or amendment
notify: FSO records system at each terminal; CySO reports the incident to the owner or operator (Chief Operating Officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: SSI (FSP or FSA extracts, network maps, vulnerability findings, the Cybersecurity Plan draft) released to unauthorized persons, for example exfiltrated in the incident
deadline: Promptly
notify: TSA or the applicable DHS component (the Coast Guard through the COTP)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if SSI was on affected systems - FSO decides with the CySO

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example truck driver names with driver license numbers in the TOS gate module, or employee records)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. 15 additional days only if good cause for delay is given to the Department in writing within the 30 days (this extension applies to the individual notice only). Delay allowed on written request of law enforcement; no notice if, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, there is no likely identity theft or financial harm (determination in writing, kept 5 years, copy to the Department within 30 days)
notify: Affected Florida residents (mail or email)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if personal information was accessed - General Counsel decides with outside counsel (POL-03 4.5)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (for example the HR and payroll SaaS, the TOS vendor or the development contractor) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company no later than 10 days after determining the breach
notify: The company (General Counsel); the company then gives the notices above
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 2 of 5 agent contracts still lack the term (POAM-019)

trigger: Affected truck drivers or employees who reside outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residency of each affected individual; apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside (Florida is the worked example above)

obligation: OSHA report of a work-related fatality or serious injury
trigger: A company employee dies, or is hospitalized as an in-patient, loses an eye or suffers an amputation, as a result of a work-related incident (for example unsafe crane or yard equipment motion during an OT incident)
deadline: Fatality: within 8 hours. In-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye: within 24 hours
notify: OSHA Area Office or 1-800-321-6742, or the OSHA online report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for company employees. Longshore labor are employed through the hiring halls; their employer reports for them. The terminal General Manager coordinates

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties (POL-03 4.7)

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Before engaging incident vendors: call the carrier's breach hotline ($15M aggregate limit, $500K retention)
notify: Carrier breach hotline; panel counsel and forensics are assigned through it
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

trigger: Security incident affecting the customer portal, EDI services or T1 vessel operations for the alliance's 3 services
deadline: Within 24 hours of confirming an incident, then daily updates while services are affected
notify: Alliance operations and vendor risk contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual. General Counsel confirms wording

obligation: Port authority and other port partners
citation: Terminal leases; terminal services agreements; port community system and data exchange agreements (contracts)
trigger: Incident affecting vessel operations, a gate, or data exchanged with partners
deadline: Per each agreement; operationally as soon as EDI or a gate is suspended
notify: Both port authorities (lease and security contacts); carriers with vessels due; both port community systems; customs data exchange service; trucking companies (portal banner or email from a clean account)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and operational. Vice President, Terminal Operations owns partner calls (POL-03 4.11)

obligation: TOS vendor incident notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: Security incident at the TOS vendor affecting the TOS software, updates or remote support
deadline: Within 72 hours per contract
notify: The company (CySO)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual. Subpart F requires vendors to notify without delay (101.650(f)(2)); amendment tracked in POAM-019

trigger: High-severity alert on monitored IT sources
deadline: Call to the Security Manager within 30 minutes
notify: Security Manager (alternate CySO), then the CySO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual. OT alerts join the MSSP workflow by 2027-01-31 (POAM-006)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Statute: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-designated rail, transit or pipeline operator
deadline: Within 24 hours
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a rail, transit or pipeline operator (N48-49-R02, R03)

citation: TSA airport and aircraft operator security program requirements (SSI)
trigger: Significant cybersecurity incident at a TSA-regulated airport or aircraft operator
deadline: Per security program (SSI; timeline not publicly verified)
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - not an airport or aircraft operator (N48-49-R04)

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a public company
deadline: Within four business days after determining materiality
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held (N48-49-R08). The PE sponsor's own reporting duties are its matter; the CEO informs the sponsor's operating partner

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services report
trigger: Covered equipment or services found in use
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts

trigger: Kaspersky covered article found in use
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
